Reference episodes

tl_episodes.Rd

Collects the reference event intervals of a ledger into episodes. An episode keeps one identifier even when gaps in observation or prediction cut it into several ledger rows, so clipping never creates extra physiological episodes. The table separates what was observed from what was not: an episode already in progress when the recording starts has onset_status = "recording_start", and one that follows unknown reference time has onset_status = "after_unknown_reference". Only episodes with onset_status = "observed" have a known onset.

Usage

tl_episodes(ledger, merge_gap = 0)

Arguments

ledger

A tl_ledger.

merge_gap

Episodes of the same record separated by known non-event time no longer than this are merged (in the ledger's time unit). Episodes separated by unknown reference time are never merged.

Value

A data frame with one row per episode: episode_id, record, start, end (span), event_time (event time on reference-known rows of the ledger), n_fragments, onset_status, offset_status, and members (original identifiers merged into this episode).

Examples

fx <- tl_fixture("acceptance")
tl_episodes(tl_ledger(fx$records, fx$reference, fx$predictions,
                      time_unit = "min"))
#>   episode_id record start end event_time n_fragments onset_status offset_status
#> 1  rec1:e001   rec1    10  20         10           1     observed      observed
#> 2  rec1:e002   rec1    40  60         20           1     observed      observed
#>     members
#> 1 rec1:e001
#> 2 rec1:e002
